Your cash and asset protection
Your assets and cash are held with other investors assets and cash but are ringfenced
and are held separately from Vanguard’s assets and cash.
Cash
Cash held within ISA and General Accounts is held as client money when required
under the FCA Rules in Vanguard’s name but separately from any account used
to hold Vanguard’s own money. Cash held within Pension Accounts is held in the
Trustee’s name and in accordance with the Scheme Rules and Applicable Regulation
is protected by being held on trust and not as client money.
For all types of account, we will deposit any cash held in one or more trust accounts
with one or more authorised banks. It will be pooled together with the money of other
investors.
Assets
All investments held within your Account will be registered: for a Pension Account,
in the name of our Trustee; and for an ISA or General Account, in the name of our

Nominee. We will be responsible for the actions and any omissions of the Nominee
and the Trustee, as applicable.
For investments within ISA and General Accounts, investments held by our Nominee
will be held as client assets in accordance with the FCA Rules. Investments registered
in the name of the Nominee are held in an account with those of other investors, on
your behalf. This means you are still the beneficial owner of your Vanguard Funds and
you will have a claim over them even if we and/ or the Nominee become insolvent.
Your investments will not be separately identifiable from those of other investors, but
we will keep a separate and up to date record of your individual entitlement. However,
in the event of our insolvency and a shortfall in the pooled account at the Nominee,
you would share pro rata with other investors in the amount of the shortfall. We have
procedures in place to carry out checks and identify any shortfall in your investments,
which we will correct if we are responsible for it.
For investments within Pension Accounts investments held by the Trustee will be held
in trust in accordance with the Scheme Rules. Investments registered in the name
of the Trustee are held in a Scheme account with those of other Members, on your
behalf. This means you are still the beneficiary of your Vanguard Funds held in your
Vanguard Personal Pension. Your investments will not be separately identifiable from
those of other Members, but we will keep a separate and up to date record of your
individual entitlement as a Member. However, in the event of our insolvency and a
shortfall in the pooled account at the Trustee, you would share pro rata with other
Members in the amount of the shortfall. We have procedures in place to carry out
checks and identify any shortfall in your investments, which we will correct if we are
responsible for it.
You have the right to request a statement of the Vanguard Funds held on your behalf
at any time, there will be no charge for this.

Your Annual Costs and Charges Statement
Section 1 – Introduction
This statement has been prepared to provide you with the costs and charges you
have paid. Please note that this information is only related to General Accounts, ISAs,
Personal Pensions and Junior ISAs. These are broken down as follows:
Account fees - these are fees paid to Vanguard for the provision of the Vanguard
Investor online service:
● One-Off Costs – These are costs you would pay when entering or exiting your
service or investment
● Ongoing Costs – These are costs we take each year for providing you the
online service and administering your investment accounts. The maximum
annual charge is £375
Cash balances held within your account may earn interest at a rate determined by
Vanguard. The current rate can be found at https://www.vanguardinvestor.co.uk/need￾help/answer/will-i-receive-interest-on-cash-held-in-my-account.
Vanguard may keep any interest that is received from your cash balance to cover
our costs and to enable us to continue to develop our products and services. Where
payable, interest is earned daily and normally paid into your account on the first
business day of each month. Vanguard does not charge an account fee for any
cash which is held in your account. Please see the Key Features Document for more
information.
This has the effect of increasing the total cost of your account.
Fund management costs – these are fees paid to Vanguard for managing the fund(s)
and associated costs. These fees are deducted from the price of the fund.
● One-Off Costs – These are costs you would pay when entering or exiting your
investment
● Ongoing Costs – These are costs taken each year by the managers of your
investments
● Transaction Costs – These are costs incurred by the managers when buying or
selling underlying investments
● Incidental Costs – This would be the impact of any performance fee
Please note that these fees are related to the period 13/02/2025 to 12/02/2026. Fund
management costs are only produced periodically and thus we display the most
recent available data. As a result of this, we have aligned the account fee dates to
match the data we have for fund management costs.

The below tables break down the cost and charges of your investments for your ISA
during this period.
Three tables are presented below to you:
● The total cost and charges against your account(s) presented both in monetary
and percentage terms of the total investment values
● The account fees and their breakdown represent the costs of administering
your investment accounts with Vanguard
● The fund management costs and their breakdown by fund show the costs that
each fund manager takes for managing the investments.
